meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'not bad'.

examples.text: Ну что же, неплохо. Ты молодец.
examples.trans: Well then, not bad. Good job.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Borrowed via German 'Pastete' from Old French/Italian 'pâté'/'pastetto', referring to finely ground seasoned meat or liver.

examples.trans: The chef prepares a signature pâté.
Chef, this is simply amazing pâté!

examples.text: Костя, быстро попробуй мой новый паштет.
examples.trans: Kostya, quickly taste my new pâté.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'consistency, texture' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У этого крем-супа должна быть нежная консистенция.
examples.trans: This cream soup must have a smooth consistency.

examples.text: Посмотри, у соуса получилась идеальная густая консистенция.
examples.trans: Look, the sauce turned out with a perfect thick texture.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'остав'). Common masculine noun meaning 'roster, lineup, composition' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And I got the ingredients right.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

подобрать.gloss: to pick up; to select, to find a match

meanings.en: to pick up from the floor or ground
meanings.note: подобрать слова = to find the right words
подобрать слова = to find the right words

examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna will pick them up.
He picked the keys up from the floor.

examples.text: Очень плохие цветы. Клавдия Викторовна подберёт.
examples.trans: Very bad flowers. Klavdia Viktorovna will pick them up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to go in, to come in, to enter
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go in', forming an aspectual pair with 'войти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left.

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево, к администратору. Там сидит такой Лисицын.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left, to the administrator. A fellow named Lisitsyn sits there.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Borrowed via French 'secret' from Latin 'secretum' (something set apart or hidden).

examples.trans: These are our little men's secrets!

examples.text: А вы кем работаете, если не секрет?
examples.trans: And what do you do, if it is not a secret?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a look', forming an aspectual pair with 'смотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch (a film) through') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'meeting' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('date (romantic)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
